answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as a crystal clear signal of commitment. This mechanism forces an attacker to acquire a marble-sized stake of the network value, which is prohibitive at scale. If an agent attempts to simulate multiple identities, the cost of acquiring the required onyx-grade collateral becomes exponentially expensive, ensuring that influence remains tied to economic skin-in-the-game rather than the ability to spawn infinite virtual agents.
